notable_absence.finding: The 'Couchstore verses Magma at a Glance' table's 'Maximum data per node' row notes Magma 128 vBuckets has '10 TB, but with much higher possibility of data imbalance' compared to plain '10 TB' for Magma 1024 vBuckets - the data-imbalance risk is asserted but never explained on this page (what causes it, how to detect it, what to do about it); the reader is left to infer it relates to fewer, larger hash buckets across the same node count, a plausible but page-unstated mechanism.

cross_component_finding: This page and memory.json (its sibling in this batch) each independently state the same two minimum memory-to-data ratios (Couchstore 10%, Magma 1%) in different wording, and this page and storage-settings.json each send the reader to the other for Magma's flushing/compaction thread settings ('See Magma Flushing and Compaction Threads for more information about these settings' here; the actual settings text lives entirely on storage-settings.md). Neither is a contradiction, but both are content-duplication/content-splitting patterns across this batch's eight pages worth a single reconciliation note rather than four separate ones.
